summary: Brick 1853 light at Brazos Santiago Pass, Port Isabel, Texas: discontinued 1888, relit 1895, decommissioned 1905; state historic site since 1950, tower open to climb.

structures.note: Heights differ: LighthouseFriends says fifty feet; THC's site page says 72-foot lighthouse; station record 17.0 m

resolved_conflicts.explanation: THC's history page says construction was under way by 1851 and the tower was completed two years later, in 1853; THC's site page says the lighthouse was built in 1852; LighthouseFriends gives construction from December 1851 and completion in early spring 1853 after the Brownsville wreck. The 1852 and 1853 dates are not reconciled by the sources and the story states both.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) lens year: LighthouseFriends dates the third-order Fresnel lens two years after the 1855 dwelling (about 1857); the station record gives 1854. (2) Height: LighthouseFriends 'fifty-foot' tower; THC site page '72-foot lighthouse' (total); station record 17.0 m. (3) Range: THC gives 'almost 16 miles' with no unit; no nautical-mile range in any source read. (4) Status: LighthouseFriends says returned to operation as a private aid in 1955; THC says not since 1905. LighthouseFriends also says the lighthouse was 'inactive for 117 years' before the 2022 ceremony. (5) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says Texas Parks and Wildlife owns it; THC says donated to the state in 1950 and runs it as a state historic site; the USLHS record lists the THC as owner and the City as manager. (6) The 1897 Board quote is taken from LighthouseFriends; the corpus volume for 1896-97 was searched for the lantern passage and did not return it, so the story attributes it to LighthouseFriends's quotation. (7) The NY Herald notice of 19 April 1853 is read only as quoted by THC. (8) The Chronicling America search for Texas papers 1853-1856 returned no hits. (9) The record's 'built 1999' (keeper's cottage) is 2000 in LighthouseFriends and the 1990s in THC. (10) The Brownsville wreck has no date in any source read. (11) Roster matched to the USLHS place by name and position (0.57 km); person slugs come from roster.py, and every roster line in the story was checked against the archive page. (12) Corpus pages: 1891-92 scan p.159 (act of 2 March 1889, 'commenced proceedings in condemnation'), 1893 scan p.163 ('still engaged in securing title'), 1894 scan p.471 (printed p.134 confirmed by the OCR header; 'it is probable that title will be vested'), 1896-97 scan p.20 ('A third-order light, July 15,1895'). Printed page numbers for the 1891-92 and 1893 entries are not confirmed by the OCR (the page index marks them '?'); the story cites scan pages. (13) THC's site page gives 1852 as the year the lighthouse was built; its history page gives completion in 1853. The story states both. (14) The lens was removed from the tower before Confederate soldiers used it as a lookout (LighthouseFriends), but no date is given for that removal. The 1905 event is the lens's shipment to Mobile, Alabama, not the removal from the tower.
